chunks: Ibn Dawud said in his Rijal — a manuscript —

(The Sheikh of the Imami theologians and jurists; their leadership in knowledge in his time culminated with him; a faqih of fine thought, subtle in intelligence, prompt in response; and his stature is greater than what any praise can express — he has nearly two hundred authored works.)

key_terms.الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: the Imamiyya — Twelver Shia Muslims who affirm the Imamate of the Twelve Imams
key_terms.رِيَاسَتُهُمْ: their leadership/headship — the intellectual and scholarly authority over the community
key_terms.شَيْخُ مُتَكَلِّمِي: Sheikh of the theologians — the supreme master of Imami scholastic theology (kalam)
key_terms.مُصَنَّفٍ: authored work — a composed/written text, indicating extraordinary prolific scholarship

ai.seo_question: What does Ibn Dawud al-Hilli say in his Rijal about the Sheikh of Imami theologians and jurists who authored nearly two hundred works?
ai.summary: This passage records Ibn Dawud al-Hilli's biographical commendation of a preeminent Imami scholar — almost certainly Sheikh al-Mufid (d. 413 AH) — identifying him as the unchallenged head of the Imamiyya's theological and juristic tradition in his era, celebrated for his mental acuity and prolific written output. The formula 'his stature is greater than what praise can express' (حاله أعظم من الثناء عليه) is a classical Arabic expression of the highest biographical commendation in rijal literature, employed when a scholar's eminence is deemed too vast to be captured by words.
